correctness.rationale: For n>=9 any connected K_{2,5}-free cograph must have a singleton root join factor, hence a universal vertex: otherwise a minimum root factor of size>=2 has complement >=5 and creates K2,5. After removing v, K1∨H avoids K2,5 iff Δ(H)<=4 and H avoids K2,4. The published K2,4 cograph structural lemma then forces every connected H-component to have <=6 vertices; its local optimal edge counts for orders 1..6 are (0,1,3,6,10,11), with the unique admissible 6-vertex 11-edge block B6=(K2⊔K1)∨(K2⊔K1). I independently enumerated all simple graphs through 6 vertices, filtered induced P4, K2,4 common-neighbor counts and Δ<=4; optimum counts agree, with 90 labeled order-6 optima (single B6 isomorphism class). The exact unbounded integer knapsack has deficits 2d-w(d)=(2,3,3,2,0,1); its residue-optimal partitions yield δ=(0,1,2,3,2), including the 3B6 alternative for residue 3; independently verified optimal deficits AND complete partition types for m=8..200, not treated as proof. The analytic deficit argument proves all m. Small n7=17, n8=20 by cotree root cases; disconnected upper 3n-6 cannot attain claimed connected bound even in δ3 residue by modular component orders. Thus formula and complete n>=9 extremizers hold.
